headline: Together AI has still not said how many customers' prompts were exposed or who was behind the leak.
summary: Check, nothing new. Re-read Together AI's security post (s001): its review of the affected data is still ongoing, it will contact affected customers directly as needed, and it names no count and no attacker (q003, q005 open). OpenRouter's Nov 22 post still says it off-boarded three providers without naming them (c016 stays Unverified). No regulator notice and no new reporting that adds a fact.

headline: Together AI says OpenRouter did not drop it; whether it was one of the three providers removed is now disputed.
summary: BleepingComputer (s011) updated its story at 1:58 PM ET Nov 24 with a Together AI statement saying OpenRouter did not remove it from the platform and that OpenRouter had not turned on zero data retention for its traffic; the story still names Together AI, Phala and Novita as the three providers dropped. OpenRouter's Together provider page (s014, Tier 1) still lists 26 models served by Together. c016 changed from Reported to Unverified (conflicting accounts); q004 answer updated. Together AI's post and the OpenRouter, Dragos, Novita, Phala, MiniMax and Atlas Cloud posts are unchanged. Still no customer count, no root-cause write-up, no attacker named and no regulator notice. headline: Phala's final report narrows its exposure window to Oct 21 to Nov 1; nothing new links it to Together AI.
summary: Added Phala's final incident report (s013, Tier 1), posted Nov 23 and replacing its Nov 10 preliminary report. Phala now says requests to one model it served on OpenRouter were readable by an attacker from Oct 21 to Nov 1, not Oct 21 to Nov 8 as first reported, and that the same attacker later reached two more of its servers. It does not mention Together AI. Updated Phala and Novita's notices and the one-attacker question (c013, c014). Together AI's post and the OpenRouter, Dragos, Novita and MiniMax posts are unchanged. Still no customer count, no root-cause write-up from Together AI, no attacker named and no regulator notice. Privacy check done: no names of people, no handles, no contact details.

headline: MiniMax says its own security system opened links in requests forwarded to it by OpenRouter and other providers.
summary: Added MiniMax's statement (s012, Tier 1), posted 8:58 PM ET Nov 23 and now linked from OpenRouter's list of provider notices. MiniMax says an automated security process pulled web links out of requests forwarded by OpenRouter and by providers including Novita, StreamLake and Atlas Cloud and opened some of them, including requests marked zero data retention; it says it kept only the links, found no evidence of prompts being passed to third parties, turned the process off and deleted the logged links (c017). It does not mention Together AI, whose cause was an exposed credential. Updated Atlas Cloud's claim, OpenRouter's notice list and the OpenRouter answer (c015, c012, q004). Together AI's post and the OpenRouter, Dragos, Novita, Phala and Atlas Cloud posts are unchanged. Still no customer count, no attacker named and no regulator notice. headline: Axios reports OpenRouter's customer emails are genuine and named three providers that forwarded requests to MiniMax.
summary: Added Axios (s010, Tier 2). It reports that a spokesperson for OpenRouter's owner, Stripe, confirmed OpenRouter's customer emails are genuine, and that the emails named three providers that forwarded requests to MiniMax (c011). It lists Together AI among at least four AI infrastructure companies with recent incidents but does not link them to one attacker (c014). Atlas Cloud's revised notice now names MiniMax M3, M2.7 and M3.1 Flash and says it is reviewing other upstream providers (c015). Fixed the OpenRouter answer to say four provider notices, not three (q004). Together AI's post is unchanged since its 12:56 AM ET Nov 22 edit. Still no customer count, no attacker named and no MiniMax statement. Privacy check done: no names of people, no handles, no contact details.

headline: Atlas Cloud posted a notice, and OpenRouter now lists four provider notices instead of three.
summary: Atlas Cloud (s009, Tier 1) says a researcher's link tests showed a third party opening prompts sent to MiniMax's official API, not on Atlas Cloud's own systems; it stopped sending requests there and took all its models off OpenRouter by its own choice. Added as c015. OpenRouter's list of provider notices now links Atlas Cloud, Novita, Phala and Together (c012 updated). Together AI's post is unchanged since its 12:56 AM ET edit. Still no customer count, no attacker named and no list of OpenRouter's three off-boarded providers. Privacy check done: no names of people, no handles, no contact details.
